briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate change expert spokesperson briefing for September 26, 2026. Today, we aim to discuss the various facets of the intensifying global climate crisis, the domestic and international efforts to combat it, and the challenges that lie ahead.

sections.title: 🔴 The Global Climate Crisis: Its Severe Impacts
sections.content: Recently, the direct impacts of the climate crisis have been intensifying in various parts of the world. Domestically, cases of aircraft performance degradation due to extreme heatwaves have been reported [1, 3]. In the Philippines, warnings have been issued that typhoon rainfall will surge to 'unprecedented levels' as a result of climate change [5]. Vietnam is experiencing both flood seasons and severe droughts, with concerns about saltwater intrusion due to El Niño [7]. The U.S. East Coast is also bracing for more powerful Nor'easter storms, intensified by climate change [20, 26]. These extreme climatic phenomena are causing difficulties for French wine-producing regions [27], negatively impacting child nutrition [25], and threatening the imminent, permanent disappearance of Papua's precious 'eternal snow' [29], thereby posing widespread threats to global ecosystems and social systems.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Steps Towards Climate Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, efforts to adapt to climate change and achieve carbon neutrality continue. In Japan, new rice varieties are emerging as a notable alternative to overcome the climate crisis, even amidst 40℃ heatwaves [2]. Domestically, activities to raise public awareness are ongoing, such as Chungju City in Chungcheongbuk-do hosting a special lecture on 'Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality' with author Lee Jeong-mo [6]. Gwangyang City received the grand prize in the administrative sector for carbon neutrality practices [9], and Siheung City is strengthening its capabilities for carbon neutrality and RE100 compliance through lectures on renewable energy transition [10]. Furthermore, Yongin Special City is guiding the final performance registration for the carbon neutrality points in the automotive sector [11], and Jeonju City is supplying balcony solar panels to 540 households, reducing electricity bills and contributing to carbon neutrality [12, 19]. Internationally, Konecranes has set a corporate climate goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 90% by 2050 [8].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Grid Investment and International Cooperation for Renewable Energy Expansion
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a core pillar of climate crisis response, and infrastructure investment and international cooperation for this are actively underway. Jeollabuk-do is making a strategic move to attract high-tech industries by focusing on grid expansion beyond just renewable energy expansion [13]. KEPCO KPS has made its first investment in overseas renewable energy by acquiring a stake in an Indonesian hydropower plant, signaling the international expansion of domestic companies [14]. The International Energy Agency (IEA) recommended grid expansion to Turkey for renewable energy growth, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure [15]. In the private sector, renewable energy investments are also active, with Valorem Group completing the refinancing of its 192MW renewable energy portfolio and pursuing large-scale financing [16]. Furthermore, 17 public institutions in Jeju Island are undergoing continuous inspections for innovative projects such as utilizing Samdasoo renewable energy and AI travel planning [17], demonstrating regional efforts in renewable energy utilization.

sections.title: ⚠️ Barriers to Climate Action and Challenges in Social Perception
sections.content: Despite efforts to address the climate crisis, many challenges and barriers still exist. A total of 888 renewable energy siting restrictions have been identified across 48 U.S. states [18], indicating physical and institutional constraints on renewable energy expansion. Furthermore, there are difficulties in social perception and communication regarding climate change. Reports suggest that while some TV meteorologists want to discuss climate change, not all viewers are willing to hear it [21]. An analysis even posited that there is a perception that it is easier to live as a climate change denier than an 'eco-warrior' [28]. These points highlight significant challenges in fostering social consensus and public participation for climate action.

sections.title: 🌍 The Importance of Technological Innovation and Research for Climate Crisis Response
sections.content: The importance of technological innovation and research to enhance the efficiency of climate crisis response is also being highlighted. While data and AI technologies have the potential to accelerate climate change action, a cautious perspective has also been presented, stating that these technologies cannot replace human efforts [22]. Burlington County, New Jersey, has been selected as an institution to conduct new climate change research [23], signaling strengthened regional scientific approaches. Furthermore, public figures from various sectors of society, such as Maggie Baird, who raised two music superstars, are joining climate action to draw public attention [24]. This demonstrates that not only technology and research but also widespread societal interest and participation are essential for overcoming the climate crisis.

briefing.closing: As we have reviewed in today's briefing, the climate crisis is intensifying globally in various forms, but simultaneously, innovative efforts and solidarity to overcome it are continuously progressing. We will continue to do our utmost to clearly communicate the scientific facts of climate change, seek practical solutions, and foster everyone's participation. This concludes today's climate briefing.
